condition.purpose: Determine whether a loan above 80.00% LTV has an eligible property type under STD-8.2, including the stated Florida restriction for Warrantable Condos.

rule.description: Determine whether the property meets the guideline's listed-for-sale timing definition.

ledger.clause:
STD-8.8 A property is considered listed for sale under §11.5 if it has been listed for sale in the last six months, measured from (a) the last date of being listed to (b) the Application Date. \[G §11.5, p. 12\]

STD-8.9 Loans on such properties will be considered under the following characteristics: the property is not in default or otherwise delinquent on lien(s); for investment properties, the subject must be occupied by a tenant and may not be vacant; the loan must qualify as either (a) ≥ 1.0 DSCR or (b) 43% maximum DTI (Q-14); a prepayment penalty of at least three (3) years is required unless the property is in a state that does not allow prepayment penalties; twenty-four (24) months of reserves are required, and cash-in-hand may be considered if otherwise consistent with the Guide; the loan must have a fully amortizing term, interest only is not available; the maximum LTV / CLTV is 65% based on the lesser of (a) appraised value or (b) lowest recent listing price; no subordinate financing is allowed; impounds are required. \[G §11.5, pp. 11–12\]

condition.purpose: Determine whether a property considered listed for sale under §11.5 meets the stated loan and property conditions.
steps: Initial Document Review: Review the listed-for-sale determination, lien status, occupancy, qualification, prepayment penalty, reserves, amortization, value, subordinate financing, and impounds information.
Eligibility Verification: Apply the conditions in STD-8.9 to a property considered listed for sale under §11.5.

Validation and Verification: Verify each applicable condition, including the 65% maximum based on the lesser of appraised value or lowest recent listing price, and the state exception for prepayment penalties.
Final Determination: Record whether all applicable STD-8.9 conditions are met.
checks: The property is not in default or otherwise delinquent on lien(s).
For an investment property, the subject is occupied by a tenant and is not vacant.
The loan qualifies as either at least 1.0 DSCR or 43% maximum DTI (Q-14).
A prepayment penalty of at least three (3) years is in place unless the property is in a state that does not allow prepayment penalties.
Reserves are 24 months; cash-in-hand may be considered if otherwise consistent with the Guide.
The loan has a fully amortizing term and is not interest only.
Maximum LTV / CLTV is 65% based on the lesser of appraised value or lowest recent listing price.
No subordinate financing is allowed.
Impounds are in place.

outcomes.criterion: The property is considered listed for sale under §11.5 and every applicable STD-8.9 condition is met.
There is no case for this outcome.
The property is considered listed for sale under §11.5 and at least one applicable STD-8.9 condition is not met.
The property is not considered listed for sale under §11.5.

condition.purpose: Determine whether the subject property meets the STD-8.1 CLTV limits and printed minimum DSCR conditions applicable to Non-Warrantable Condo, Condotel / PUDtel, 2-4 Unit, or Manufactured Home.
steps: Initial Document Review: Review the property type, loan purpose, CLTV, state, and DSCR information available for the case.
Eligibility Verification: Identify the applicable STD-8.1 row and transaction purpose; do not apply this job when the property type is not one of the types covered by the printed caps.

Validation and Verification: Compare CLTV with the applicable printed cap. For Non-Warrantable Condo and Condotel / PUDtel in Florida, apply the printed -5% CLTV condition. For those two property types, verify the printed Min DSCR: 1.0 condition.
Final Determination: Record whether every applicable printed cap and minimum DSCR condition is met.
checks: For a Non-Warrantable Condo, CLTV does not exceed 80% for Purchase, 75% for Refi R/T, or 75% for Refi C/O; for Florida properties, apply the printed -5% CLTV condition.
For a Condotel / PUDtel, CLTV does not exceed 75% for Purchase, 70% for Refi R/T, or 65% for Refi C/O; for Florida properties, apply the printed -5% CLTV condition.
For a 2-4 Unit property, CLTV does not exceed 80%.
For a Manufactured Home, CLTV does not exceed 65% for Purchase, 60% for Refi R/T, or 60% for Refi C/O.
For a Non-Warrantable Condo or Condotel / PUDtel, DSCR is at least 1.0.

outcomes.criterion: The property type is covered by this job and every applicable printed CLTV cap and minimum DSCR condition is met.
There is no case for this outcome.
The property type is covered by this job and an applicable printed CLTV cap or minimum DSCR condition is not met.
The property type is not Non-Warrantable Condo, Condotel / PUDtel, 2-4 Units, or Manufactured.

condition.purpose: Determine whether a vacant property's cash-out refinance meets the conditions stated in STD-8.7.
steps: Initial Document Review: Review vacancy status, loan purpose, loan amount, CLTV, representative credit score, DSCR, prepayment penalty, interest-only status, escrow status, reserves, and ownership months.

Eligibility Verification: Apply this job to a vacant property's cash-out refinance and verify the printed score, DSCR, prepayment penalty, interest-only, impounds, reserves, CLTV, and ownership conditions.
Validation and Verification: Obtain Acra confirmation for loans of $1,500,000 or more and for how the 15 months of ownership are measured.
Final Determination: Record whether the printed conditions are met and whether requested confirmations remain outstanding.
checks: For a vacant property's cash-out refinance, representative FICO score is at least 700.
For a vacant property's cash-out refinance, DSCR is at least 1.15.
For a vacant property's cash-out refinance, a prepayment penalty of at least 3 years is in place where allowable.
For a vacant property's cash-out refinance, the loan is not interest-only.
For a vacant property's cash-out refinance, impounds are in place.
For a vacant property's cash-out refinance, reserves are at least 6 months.
For a vacant property's cash-out refinance with a loan amount under $1,500,000, CLTV does not exceed 60%; obtain Acra confirmation for loans of $1,500,000 or more.
For a vacant property's cash-out refinance, ownership is at least 15 months; obtain Acra confirmation on how the 15 months are measured.

outcomes.criterion: The property is vacant, the transaction is a cash-out refinance, all applicable printed conditions are met, and any requested Acra confirmations have been obtained.
The property is vacant and the transaction is a cash-out refinance, but Acra confirmation for a loan of $1,500,000 or more or for how the 15 months of ownership are measured remains outstanding.
The property is vacant, the transaction is a cash-out refinance, and a printed condition is not met.
The property is not vacant or the transaction is not a cash-out refinance.

missing_reads: The DSCR ratio; prepayment penalty duration and whether it is allowable; Acra confirmation for loans of $1,500,000 or more; Acra confirmation on how the 15 months of ownership are measured.

STD-8.6 Rate and term refinance of a vacant property (§10.17): minimum 700 FICO score; maximum \$1,000,000 to maximum 70% CLTV; maximum \$2,000,000 to maximum 65% CLTV; minimum 1.000 DSCR or maximum 40.0% DTI (Q-14); minimum two-year prepayment penalty (where allowable); full amortization required, no interest-only programs; impounds required; minimum six months reserves. The Summary states the same conditions with “Max CLTV 70% for loan amounts under \$1,000,000 and 65% for loan amounts under \$2,000,000”. Treatment at exactly \$1,000,000 and \$2,000,000: Acra confirmation requested → Q-10. \[G §10.17, p. 11; S: Occupancy Type\]

The Summary states: minimum 700 FICO; DSCR ≥ 1.15; ≥ 3-year PPP (where allowable); no interest only; impounds required; 6 months reserves; “Max CLTV 60% for loan amounts under \$1,500,000”; “Requires ≥15 months ownership”. Loans of \$1,500,000 or more, and how the 15 months are measured: Acra confirmation requested → Q-10. \[S: Occupancy Type; G §10.17, p. 11\]

condition.purpose: Determine whether a vacant property's rate and term refinance meets STD-8.6, and identify conditions requiring Acra confirmation.
steps: Initial Document Review: Review vacancy status, loan purpose, loan amount, CLTV, representative credit score, qualification method and ratios, prepayment penalty, interest-only status, escrow status, and reserves.

Eligibility Verification: Apply this job to a vacant property's rate and term refinance; verify the printed score, CLTV, qualification, prepayment penalty, amortization, impounds, and reserves conditions.

Validation and Verification: For loan amounts at exactly $1,000,000 or $2,000,000, obtain Acra confirmation as requested. Resolve the stated qualifying alternative of minimum 1.000 DSCR or maximum 40.0% DTI (Q-14).
Final Determination: Record whether the printed conditions are met and whether any requested confirmation remains outstanding.
checks: For a vacant property's rate and term refinance, representative FICO score is at least 700.

For a vacant property's rate and term refinance, the applicable CLTV limit is met: maximum $1,000,000 to maximum 70% CLTV; maximum $2,000,000 to maximum 65% CLTV; obtain Acra confirmation for treatment at exactly $1,000,000 and $2,000,000.
For a vacant property's rate and term refinance, minimum 1.000 DSCR or maximum 40.0% DTI is met (Q-14).
For a vacant property's rate and term refinance, a minimum two-year prepayment penalty is in place where allowable.
For a vacant property's rate and term refinance, full amortization is in place and the loan is not interest-only.
For a vacant property's rate and term refinance, impounds are in place.
For a vacant property's rate and term refinance, reserves are at least six months.

outcomes.criterion: The property is vacant, the transaction is a rate and term refinance, all applicable printed conditions are met, and any required Acra confirmation has been obtained.
The property is vacant and the transaction is a rate and term refinance, but Acra confirmation for treatment at exactly $1,000,000 or $2,000,000, or the Q-14 alternative, remains unresolved.
The property is vacant, the transaction is a rate and term refinance, and a printed condition is not met.
The property is not vacant or the transaction is not a rate and term refinance.

condition.purpose: Determine whether, when gifting is used, the applicant contributes a minimum of 10% of the purchase price from their own sourced and seasoned funds.
steps: Step 1 - Initial Document Review: Review available bank statements and other funds-to-close documentation for the applicant's own funds and any gift funds.
Step 2 - Eligibility Verification: Determine whether gifting is used and identify the applicant's own contribution to the transaction.

Step 3 - Validation and Verification: Verify that the applicant's own sourced and seasoned funds contributed are at least 10% of the purchase price. Gift documentation requirements are in the Seller's Guide gift-fund section (Appendix B).
Step 4 - Final Determination: Determine whether the own-funds contribution requirement is met when gifting is used.
checks: When gifting is used, the applicant contributes a minimum of 10% of the purchase price consisting of their own sourced and seasoned funds.

STD-1.10 Minimum loan amount \$100,000; maximum loan amount \$3,000,000; loan amount to be in \$50 increments. \[S: Loan Amount\]

STD-1.11 Seller concession / other contributions: limited to 3% of the sale price. \[S: Loan Amount\]

STD-1.12 Gifting is allowed and “requires borrower to contribute a minimum of 10% of the purchase price consisting of their own funds”; §8.7 states the contribution as the applicant's “own sourced and seasoned funds”. Gift documentation requirements are in the Seller's Guide gift-fund section, not reproduced (Appendix B). \[S: Loan Amount; G §8.7, p. 12\]

STD-9.1 Gift funds, investment property or second homes: applicant(s) are required to contribute a portion of their own sourced and seasoned funds to the transaction at a minimum of 10% of the purchase price. Gift documentation requirements are in the Seller's Guide gift-fund section (Appendix B). \[G §8.7, p. 12; S: Loan Amount\]

STD-9.2 Verification of the seasoning of funds to close is required on loans over 70% CLTV for consumer transactions, or business purpose loans where funds to close are over \$50,000 and over 70% CLTV. Whether any loan on this program is a consumer transaction: Acra confirmation requested → Q-27. \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

STD-9.3 Where the account(s) serving as the source of funds must be verified, verification may include a copy of the borrower's bank statement(s) for the most recent month(s), or a VOD reflecting a current and average balance for the most recent month(s). \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

STD-9.4 “All transactions require a minimum of 30-days documentation.” Whether any seasoning period applies to domestic funds beyond this documentation minimum: Acra confirmation requested → Q-12. \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

STD-9.5 “In contrast to the above, but consistent with §3.10.1 of this Guide, funds held in a foreign bank / currency will need to be repatriated at minimum three (3) business days prior to Closing and Foreign Nationals, regardless of LTV / CLTV, need to document a minimum of 60 days seasoning.” Whether the repatriation requirement applies to any borrower holding funds abroad or only to foreign nationals, and what evidence applies: Acra confirmation requested → Q-12. \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

condition.purpose: Determine whether funds-to-close seasoning verification is required under STD-9.2.
steps: Step 1 - Initial Document Review: Review the loan application and available transaction information to identify the transaction type and funds to close.

Step 4 - Final Determination: Determine whether the seasoning verification requirement is triggered.
checks: Seasoning verification is required when the loan is a consumer transaction with CLTV over 70%, or a business purpose loan with funds to close over $50,000 and CLTV over 70%.

condition.purpose: Determine whether the required entity documentation has been provided and meets the stated requirements.
steps: Step 1 - Initial Document Review: Obtain and review the applicable entity_documents. Do not accept borrower letters stating that required documents are not required, available, or excused from providing them.

Step 2 - Eligibility Verification: Identify which stated documentation requirements apply to the entity type and transaction, including any alternative documentation expressly stated for unavailable stock certificates or stock ledgers.

Step 3 - Validation and Verification: Verify that the required formation documents and amendments, governing documents and amendments, ownership evidence, applicable stock records or alternatives, name-matching or explanation, good-standing or equivalent certificate, applicable foreign qualification, EIN/TIN evidence or submitted exception request, and unanimous written consent or board resolution are present and meet their stated requirements. Review any required Power of Attorney for a personal guarantee and any additional supporting documentation requested by Legal.

Step 4 - Final Determination: Determine whether the applicable required entity documentation is complete and meets the stated requirements; refer any EIN exception request for review by Acra's Legal Department.
checks: The complete, legible Certificate of Formation / Articles of Organization and all amendments thereto are provided.

The complete, legible Operating Agreement for LLCs and Partnerships, or Bylaws for corporations, including all referenced exhibits and amendments, states whether the entity is member or manager managed, contains authorization to borrow money and enter into contracts for mortgage assets, and designates signers; any conflict with formation documents is addressed with any additional information required.

Documentation evidencing all ownership interests is provided: for LLCs and Partnerships, the Operating Agreement identifies or attaches as an exhibit all persons by name with their ownership interest, or membership interest certificates / units in compliance with the Operating Agreement are provided.

For S or C Corporations, shareholder / stockholder certificates that comply with the Bylaws, if any, or the corporation's stock ledger when certificates are lost or unavailable, account for all outstanding shares noted in the Certificate of Formation / Articles of Organization, including those held by the corporation; when stock certificates are lost, destroyed, mutilated, or otherwise unavailable, an Affidavit of Lost Stock Certificate is provided.

For S-corporations or Partnerships where both stock certificate and stock ledger are unavailable, the most recent preceding tax year's K-1 statement for all members with 20% or more interest and a CPA or Tax Preparer letter affirming current ownership interest are provided; if the preceding year's taxes have not been filed, the letter includes a statement to that effect.
Names on entity documents match identification, or a letter of explanation addresses any discrepancy.
A Certificate of Good Standing or equivalent document valid within ninety (90) days of the closing date is provided.

A Certificate of Foreign Qualification or other qualification to operate in the state where business is conducted is provided if the entity is formed in a state other than where business is performed or where the property is located.

IRS Form SS4 or Federal Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) or Employer Identification Number (EIN) issuance letter is provided, or an EIN exception request with a letter of explanation stating the applicable grounds is submitted for review by Acra's Legal Department.

A Unanimous Written Consent / Board Resolution signed by all members regardless of their percentage of interest authorizes the transaction with Acra Lending and identifies who is authorized to sign the loan documents on behalf of and to bind the entity; it is not used to designate a signor on a personal guarantee.
A Power of Attorney is utilized by the principal to designate an attorney in fact to execute a personal guarantee when required.

6.2 Entity documentation
STD-6.10 The documents below are required, without exception, and borrower letters stating that they are not required, available, or excused from providing such documents are not acceptable. \[G §3.12, pp. 8–9\]

- Complete, legible copy of the Certificate of Formation / Articles of Organization and all amendments thereto.

- Complete (with all referenced exhibits), legible copy of the Operating Agreement for LLCs and Partnerships, or Bylaws for corporations, and all amendments, that states whether the entity is member or manager managed, contains authorization to borrow money and enter into contracts for mortgage assets, and designates signers. Additional information may be required if the formation documents and the Operating Agreement or Bylaws conflict.

- All documentation evidencing ownership interests: for LLCs and Partnerships, the Operating Agreement must identify, or attach as an exhibit, all persons by name with their ownership interest, or provide copies of the membership interest certificates / units in compliance with the Operating Agreement.

- For S or C Corporations: shareholder / stockholder certificates that comply with the Bylaws, if any, or, if stock certificates are lost or unavailable, the corporation's stock ledger. The certificate or ledger must account for all outstanding shares noted in the Certificate of Formation / Articles of Organization, including those held by the corporation. If stock certificates are lost, destroyed, mutilated, or otherwise unavailable, an Affidavit of Lost Stock Certificate is required.

- For S-corporations or Partnerships, where both stock certificate and stock ledger are unavailable: (i) the most recent preceding tax year's K-1 statement for all members with 20% or more interest, and (ii) a letter from the CPA or Tax Preparer affirming current ownership interest, with a statement to that effect if the preceding year's taxes have not been filed.

6.2 Entity documentation
- Names on the entity documents must match the identification; if they do not match exactly, a letter of explanation is required to address the discrepancy.

- Certificate of Good Standing or equivalent document valid within ninety (90) days of the closing date.

- Certificate of Foreign Qualification or other qualification to operate in the state where business is being conducted, if the entity is formed in a state other than where business is performed or where the property is located.

- IRS Form SS4 or Federal Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) or Employer Identification Number (EIN) issuance letter for the entity. EIN exception requests may be submitted for review by Acra's Legal Department with a letter of explanation stating the applicable grounds.

- A Unanimous Written Consent / Board Resolution signed by all members regardless of their percentage of interest, (i) authorizing the transaction with Acra Lending and (ii) identifying who is authorized to sign the loan documents on behalf of and to bind the entity. It may be required by the Operating Agreement or Bylaws even where ownership is held by one individual. It cannot be used to designate a signor on a personal guarantee, only an authorized signor for the loan documents signed by the entity.

- A Power of Attorney must be utilized by the principal to designate an attorney in fact to execute a personal guarantee; see §23.5(C), not reproduced (Appendix B).

- Legal reserves the right to condition for additional supporting documentation as determined in its sole discretion.

6.1 Entity eligibility and guarantees
STD-6.1 Business Entities are eligible for financing on business purpose transactions (investment properties exclusively). \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.2 Acra will lend to, and require that title to the collateral be held, either (i) directly by an individual person(s) or (ii) by an entity acceptable to Acra in its sole discretion. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.3 Acra requires all individuals with direct or indirect ownership ≥ 20% to provide a recourse guarantee (Acra approved, or Exhibit 7) in the case of an entity borrower. All recourse is joint and several in the case of multiple guarantors. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.4 An entity borrower must be a single purpose entity (SPE): “an entity with no assets other than residential investment or rental properties; engaged in the business of owning and operating residential investment or rental properties.” Series limited liability companies are not allowed. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.5 All entities that will hold direct ownership of the subject property and will be on title as a direct owner are required to be a borrowing entity. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.6 Changes to the operating agreement or bylaws with the intent of changing ownership percentages to circumvent required personal guarantors will not be considered. “Lookback to changes cannot occur within 30 days prior to an Application Date or throughout the application process as these changes will not be recognized by Acra Lending.” \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.7 Entity / guarantor types allowed: Domestic Corporations (C and S Corp); single purpose Limited Liability Companies (LLC), excluding series LLC; Limited Liability Partnership (LLP); Limited Liability Limited Partnership (LLLP); General Partnership (GP); Limited Partnership (LP); and Sole Proprietorship. “In all events, the Borrower must be a US formed and based Entity, foreign entities (i.e.: entities formed or based outside the US) or foreign owned entities are not allowed.” \[G §3.12, p. 8\]

6.1 Entity eligibility and guarantees
STD-6.8 Not allowed: Cooperatives, Irrevocable Trusts, Land Trusts, IRAs, Non-Profit, and Joint Ventures. “Business entity nesting is limited to only one (1) wholly-owned subsidiary that in turn must be owned by individual(s); multiple nesting or ownership by multiple entities, trusts, etcetera are not acceptable.” An illustration of the permitted structure: Acra confirmation requested → Q-22. \[G §3.12, p. 8\]

STD-6.9 Acra requires at least one guarantor to have prior homeownership experience. At least one (1) borrower / guarantor on the loan must attest on the application that they are not a first-time homebuyer; if prior home ownership is not evident within the loan file, the underwriter reserves the right to condition for supporting documentation. See Q-09. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

condition.purpose: Determine whether title vesting in an inter vivos revocable trust is permitted under the stated requirements.
steps: Step 1 - Initial Document Review: Review the trust document or Certification of Trust and the loan file for the trust’s terms, trustors, trustees, beneficiaries, and any Acra Senior Management written exception.

Step 2 - Eligibility Verification: Determine whether the trust is inter vivos and revocable and whether the stated requirements for its establishment, beneficiaries, trustees, and title vesting are met.

Step 3 - Validation and Verification: Verify the required trust information and provisions, validity under the laws of the state in which it is established, and any written exception required when the Trustor(s) and Trustee(s) are not the same. Review any additional supporting documentation conditioned for by Legal.
Step 4 - Final Determination: Determine whether title vesting in the trust meets all stated requirements.
checks: A complete, legible copy of the Trust or a Certification of Trust states the existence and date of the Trust; the Trustor(s) and current Trustee(s); the powers of the Trustee; whether the Trust is revocable and, if revocable, who holds the right to revoke; the names and number of Trustees required to sign; the Trust identification number (a Social Security number or an IRS-issued Tax Identification Number); how title to Trust assets should be taken; and that the Trust has not been revoked, modified, or amended in any manner.
The Trust is valid under the laws of the state in which it is established.
The Trust is revocable, meaning it can be changed or canceled at any time for any reason during a Trustor's lifetime.
The Trust is established by one or more natural persons, solely or jointly (Grantor, Trustor, or Settlor), and becomes effective during the lifetime of the person(s) establishing it.
The primary beneficiary of the Trust is the individual(s) establishing the Trust.
Written exception by Acra Senior Management is obtained if the Trustor(s) and Trustee(s) are not the same.

The Trust specifies that the Trustee has the power to hold title and mortgage the property; that the beneficiary does not need to grant written consent for the Trust to borrow money, or that such consent has been granted in writing for purposes of the mortgage; that there is no unusual risk or impairment to the lender's rights; and that holding title in the Trust does not diminish the lender's rights as a creditor.
Any additional supporting documentation conditioned for by Legal is provided.

outcomes.criterion: Every applicable trust check holds and no required additional supporting documentation remains outstanding.
A required trust provision, written exception, or additional supporting documentation remains to be provided or cleared.
An applicable trust check does not hold.
Title is not vested in an inter vivos revocable trust.

STD-6.13 Title vesting in an inter vivos revocable trust is permitted when all of the following requirements are followed. \[G §3.12, pp. 9–10\]

- A complete, legible copy of the Trust, or a Certification of Trust stating: the existence and date of the Trust; the Trustor(s) and the current Trustee(s); the powers of the Trustee; whether the Trust is revocable and, if revocable, who holds the right to revoke; the names and number of the Trustees required to sign on behalf of the Trust; the Trust identification number (a Social Security number or an IRS-issued Tax Identification Number); how title to the Trust assets should be taken; and a statement that the Trust has not been revoked, modified, or amended in any manner.

- The Trust must be valid under the laws of the state in which it is established.

- The Trust must be revocable, meaning it can be changed or canceled at any time for any reason during a Trustor's lifetime. Irrevocable trust is not permitted.

- The Trust must be established by one or more natural persons, solely or jointly (Grantor, Trustor, or Settlor), and must become effective during the lifetime of the person(s) establishing it.

- The primary beneficiary of the Trust must be the individual(s) establishing the Trust.

- Written exception by Acra Senior Management must be obtained if the Trustor(s) and Trustee(s) are not the same.

- The Trust must specify that the Trustee has the power to hold title and mortgage the property; that the beneficiary does not need to grant written consent for the Trust to borrow money, or that such consent has been granted in writing for purposes of the mortgage; that there is no unusual risk or impairment to the lender's rights; and that holding title in the Trust does not diminish the lender's rights as a creditor.

- Legal reserves the right to condition for additional supporting documentation as determined in its sole discretion.

ledger.clause:
6.1 Entity eligibility and guarantees
STD-6.1 Business Entities are eligible for financing on business purpose transactions (investment properties exclusively). \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.2 Acra will lend to, and require that title to the collateral be held, either (i) directly by an individual person(s) or (ii) by an entity acceptable to Acra in its sole discretion. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.3 Acra requires all individuals with direct or indirect ownership ≥ 20% to provide a recourse guarantee (Acra approved, or Exhibit 7) in the case of an entity borrower. All recourse is joint and several in the case of multiple guarantors. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.4 An entity borrower must be a single purpose entity (SPE): “an entity with no assets other than residential investment or rental properties; engaged in the business of owning and operating residential investment or rental properties.” Series limited liability companies are not allowed. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.5 All entities that will hold direct ownership of the subject property and will be on title as a direct owner are required to be a borrowing entity. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.6 Changes to the operating agreement or bylaws with the intent of changing ownership percentages to circumvent required personal guarantors will not be considered. “Lookback to changes cannot occur within 30 days prior to an Application Date or throughout the application process as these changes will not be recognized by Acra Lending.” \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.7 Entity / guarantor types allowed: Domestic Corporations (C and S Corp); single purpose Limited Liability Companies (LLC), excluding series LLC; Limited Liability Partnership (LLP); Limited Liability Limited Partnership (LLLP); General Partnership (GP); Limited Partnership (LP); and Sole Proprietorship. “In all events, the Borrower must be a US formed and based Entity, foreign entities (i.e.: entities formed or based outside the US) or foreign owned entities are not allowed.” \[G §3.12, p. 8\]

condition.purpose: Determine whether the bankruptcy or foreclosure seasoning and CLTV meet the printed restrictions.
steps: Step 1 - Initial Document Review: Review credit and borrower records for bankruptcy or foreclosure and the seasoning as printed.

Step 2 - Eligibility Verification: Apply the U51 table: ≥ 36 Mo means No Restrictions; 24-35 Mo means 80% Purchase or 75% Refi R/T, Refi C/O; 12-23 Mo means 65% for either; < 12 Mo is Ineligible for either.
Step 3 - Validation and Verification: Compare the applicable seasoning, loan purpose, and CLTV with the table.
Step 4 - Final Determination: Record whether the applicable printed restriction is met.
checks: The bankruptcy or foreclosure seasoning is not in an Ineligible category and CLTV does not exceed the applicable printed maximum.

outcomes.criterion: Seasoning is ≥ 36 Mo, or is within an applicable printed CLTV maximum and is not Ineligible.
There is no case for this outcome.
Seasoning is < 12 Mo, or CLTV exceeds the applicable printed maximum.
The borrower has not had a bankruptcy or foreclosure.

condition.purpose: Verify the required documentation of mortgage or rental history, including the stated DSCR-loan property scope.
steps: Step 1 - Initial Document Review: Review reported mortgages and available housing-history documents for properties the borrower owns and / or rents over the last twelve (12) months.

Step 2 - Eligibility Verification: Consider all reported mortgages on credit. Where mortgages are not reported, determine whether the file documents history on the applicant's primary residence(s), any secondary residence(s), and the subject property. For DSCR loans, apply the stated documentation scope: subject property, principal residence, and second home (if any) of the borrower and / or guarantor(s); additional properties need not be documented unless file documents suggest a major credit event has occurred.

Step 3 - Validation and Verification: For DSCR loans, verify payment history for the primary residence, subject property, and second homes, if applicable; assess any additional-property documentation when the file suggests a major credit event.
Step 4 - Final Determination: Record whether the documentation required by the applicable scope is present.
checks: Required housing-history documentation for the applicable loan and property scope is present.

citations: Acra_DSCR_Standard_Consolidated_Guidelines_v1_0.docx#7.2 Mortgage / rental rating and payment history

check_units: Acra_DSCR_Standard_Consolidated_Guidelines_v1_0.docx#7.2 Mortgage / rental rating and payment history

ledger.clause:
STD-7.6 The mortgage / rental rating for determining mortgage pricing is determined by evaluating the ratings for properties the borrower owns and / or rents over the last twelve (12) months. All reported mortgages on credit should be considered; where the applicant has mortgages that are not reported, the file should contain documentation to evaluate history on the applicant's primary residence(s), any secondary residence(s), and the subject property. \[G §4.15, p. 5\]

STD-7.7 DSCR loans only require documentation on the subject property, principal residence, and second home (if any) of the borrower and / or guarantor(s). Additional properties do not require housing history to be documented unless documents in the file suggest a major credit event has occurred, for example a foreclosure listing the borrower (individually or as guarantor) on the credit report. For DSCR loans, the payment history is required for the primary residence, subject property, and second homes, if applicable. \[G §4.15, p. 5; §6.7, p. 6\]

STD-7.8 Loans that have matured are rated based on the maturity date of the loan; any extensions of the maturity date must be in writing. \[G §4.15, p. 5\]

ledger.clause:
STD-7.6 The mortgage / rental rating for determining mortgage pricing is determined by evaluating the ratings for properties the borrower owns and / or rents over the last twelve (12) months. All reported mortgages on credit should be considered; where the applicant has mortgages that are not reported, the file should contain documentation to evaluate history on the applicant's primary residence(s), any secondary residence(s), and the subject property. \[G §4.15, p. 5\]

STD-7.7 DSCR loans only require documentation on the subject property, principal residence, and second home (if any) of the borrower and / or guarantor(s). Additional properties do not require housing history to be documented unless documents in the file suggest a major credit event has occurred, for example a foreclosure listing the borrower (individually or as guarantor) on the credit report. For DSCR loans, the payment history is required for the primary residence, subject property, and second homes, if applicable. \[G §4.15, p. 5; §6.7, p. 6\]

STD-7.8 Loans that have matured are rated based on the maturity date of the loan; any extensions of the maturity date must be in writing. \[G §4.15, p. 5\]

condition.purpose: Determine whether CLTV is within the maximum printed for the mortgage-history label and loan purpose.
steps: Step 1 - Initial Document Review: Review the credit report for the printed mortgage-history label.

Step 2 - Eligibility Verification: Apply the U51 table maximum for the label and the applicable Purchase or Refi R/T, Refi C/O column: 1x30x12 is 80% or 75%; 0x60x12 is 75% or 70%; 0x90x12 is 65% or 65%; 0x120x12 is Ineligible or Ineligible.
Step 3 - Validation and Verification: Compare the case CLTV and loan purpose with the applicable table entry.
Step 4 - Final Determination: Record whether the applicable maximum is met and whether the printed label is Ineligible.
checks: The loan is not in a printed Ineligible category and CLTV does not exceed the maximum for the applicable mortgage-history label and loan purpose.

condition.purpose: For a tenant occupied property, require the stated rental-payment documentation when the Applicant has had forbearance or mortgage lates within the last 12-months.
steps: Step 1 - Initial Document Review: Review available credit and rental-payment evidence for forbearance or mortgage lates within the last 12-months and whether the property is tenant occupied.

Step 2 - Eligibility Verification: If the stated trigger applies, determine whether documentation is present for either timely receipt for the prior two (2) months rental payments or 12-months of subject's payment in reserve, which may be from transaction's cash-in-hand.

Step 4 - Final Determination: Record whether the applicable documentation requirement is met; do not resolve whether “Applicant” includes guarantors of an entity borrower, which is unresolved in the source.

ledger.clause:
STD-7.1 Applicants with scores from 3 repositories: acceptable with no tradeline overlay. \[S: Credit Requirements\]

STD-7.2 Applicants with 2 or fewer scores: 2 tradelines & 24 month history, or 3 tradelines & 12 month history, acceptable with no tradeline overlay. \[S: Credit Requirements\]

STD-7.3 1 or No Score / Deficient Tradelines — three entries as printed: Max 65% LTV/CLTV; DSCR Ratio ≥ 1.1; 24mos 0x30 housing history. Also as printed: “1 Reported Score: Use Actual to Max 700; No Score: Price as 700 Tier”. \[S: Credit Requirements\]

4.1 Citizenship types and limits
STD-4.1 Eligible borrower citizenship types: US Citizen, Permanent Resident, Non-Permanent Resident, Foreign National, ITIN. \[S: Borrower Citizenship\]

STD-4.2 Permanent Resident must have an unexpired PRA ID and SSA card / SSA-89. \[S: Borrower Citizenship\]

STD-4.3 Non-Permanent Resident must have proof of legal residency, which may include an unexpired employment authorization document (EAD) or valid visa. Limit printed as “Max Loan Amount: \$1.5M: Max CLTV 80%” — whether this is two independent limits or one conditional limit: Acra confirmation requested → Q-21. \[S: Borrower Citizenship\]

STD-4.4 Foreign National: “Borrowers whose Primary Residence is not located in the United States of America.” Maximum CLTV 70% (purchase) and 65% (refinance — rate & term and cash-out); “Price loan at FICO equal to 700”. No maximum loan amount is stated for foreign nationals: Acra confirmation requested → Q-21. Program documentation is in section 5. \[S: Borrower Citizenship\]

STD-4.5 ITIN: “ITIN is defined as any non-resident that is unable to provide any of the ‘Non-Permanent Resident Alien’ documents listed above.” Maximum loan amount \$1.0M; minimum FICO 640; maximum CLTV by FICO as printed below. §3.10 separately admits ITIN holders under the foreign-national program when they reside outside the US. Whether a US-resident ITIN holder is eligible, and whether the tier printed “FICO 700” means 700 and above: Acra confirmation requested → Q-03. \[S: Borrower Citizenship; G §3.10, p. 6\]

ledger.clause:
1.1 Occupancy, purpose and qualification
STD-1.7 “A 1007 will always be required on DSCR transactions – for avoidance of doubt, even on No Ratio DSCR”. Whether a Form 1025 satisfies this for a 2-4 unit property: Acra confirmation requested → Q-08. \[G §5.32, p. 3; §14.12, p. 4\]

STD-1.8 All borrowers purchasing or refinancing a one- to four-family investment property must execute a One- to Four-Family Rider with the loan documents and provide rent loss insurance coverage per §23.40 (STD-8.11 to 8.14). \[G §3.41, p. 11\]

STD-1.9 Only the subject property, principal residence and second homes are required to be listed on the application or Schedule of Real Estate Owned. \[G §5.32, p. 3; §4.15, p. 5\]

3.3 Rent schedules and rent evidence
STD-3.9 Acra requires the Single-Family Comparable Rent Schedule (FNMA Form 1007) for single family properties on (i) all DSCR qualifying files, (ii) lease-option purchase transactions where the down payment required in §3.45 is generated from excess monthly rent contributions, or (iii) when proposed rental income is being used to qualify. \[G §14.12, p. 4\]

STD-3.10 A 1007 may be from the original appraiser or any state licensed appraiser. \[G §14.12, p. 4\]

STD-3.11 Single family investment properties with excessive monthly rent payments reflected on the lease require documentation supporting that the monthly rent is typical for the area; acceptable documentation may include classified ads from local newspapers, a 1007 completed by the appraiser, or a market rent survey completed by a local real estate company or rental management company familiar with the market rents in the area. \[G §14.12, p. 4\]

STD-3.12 Short-term rental, appraisal form: for properties occupied as a short-term rental, an STRpro or similar appraisal form is acceptable as replacement to a 1007 as long as it is signed by an appropriately licensed appraiser. \[G §14.13, p. 4\]

STD-3.13 Short-term rental, actual rents: “Acra can accept short term rentals with 12-month ledgers from condotel management companies, property managers, AirBnB, VRBO, etcetera as documentation for actual rents.” How a 12-month ledger establishes qualifying rent, and how the receipt and lease conditions of STD-3.6 apply to short-term rentals: Acra confirmation requested → Q-02. \[G §5.32, p. 3; §14.13, p. 4\]

STD-3.14 Short-term rental caps: “Properties qualifying with short-term rentals are limited to 75% & 70% LTV / CLTV for Purchase or Refinance transactions respectively”; the Summary states maximum CLTV 75% (purchase) and 70% (refinance — rate & term and cash-out), minimum FICO 640. \[G §5.32, p. 3; S: Occupancy Type\]

STD-3.19 “File can qualify without calculating a DSCR Ratio to a maximum LTV / CLTV as described on the appropriate program matrix depending on FICO and other requirement. Requires 1007; however, DSCR is not calculated.” The Summary's No Ratio caps and minimum FICO are STD-3.17. \[G §5.33, p. 3; S: Income Documentation\]

STD-3.20 “Proof of actual rents is not required. Property may be short-term rental or long-term rental (appropriate pricing applies).” \[G §5.33, p. 3\]

STD-3.21 Whether No Ratio is available where another condition carries its own minimum DSCR (STD-3.16 and the table above): Acra confirmation requested → Q-13. Whether the short-term-rental caps apply to a No Ratio file: Acra confirmation requested → Q-02.

STD-3.22 Rent loss insurance applies to No Ratio DSCR (STD-8.12). \[G §23.40, p. 13\]

ledger.clause:
STD-3.1 “Acra calculates the DSCR by dividing (a) the lesser of (i) annual in-place rent or (ii) market rent (reference §14.14) by (b) the sum of annual principal, interest, real estate taxes, property insurance, and homeowner's / condominium association fees (collectively, ‘PITIA’). Subordinate financing, if applicable, would also be included in the denominator for the sake of this calculation.” \[G §5.32, p. 3\]

STD-3.2 “Acra calculates the DSCR utilizing the first payment due under the terms of the Note.” §7.5 defines Interest Only payments as “the amount sufficient to pay the accrued interest to the mortgage on a monthly basis at the time of origination”, while the §5.32 denominator lists “annual principal, interest …”. Which payment enters the DSCR denominator on an interest-only loan: Acra confirmation requested → Q-26. \[G §7.5, p. 13; §5.32, p. 3\]

STD-3.3 The reference to subordinate financing in the denominator is a calculation rule; it does not itself establish that a subordinate lien is permitted. Whether and when subordinate financing is permitted: Acra confirmation requested → Q-18. \[G §5.32, p. 3\]

STD-3.4 §14.14 (market rent), referenced in the formula, is not reproduced in the excerpt (Appendix B). \[G §5.32, p. 3\]

STD-3.5 Formula: the lesser of annual in-place rent or market rent (STD-3.1). \[G §5.32, p. 3\]

STD-3.6 Note in the same section: “Acra may use the higher of actual or market rents. Where actual rents exceed market rents, then evidence of actual rents must be documented via two (2) consecutive months proof of rental income receipt and lease agreement(s) to continue at a minimum of three (3) months after closing. Note: Security Deposit does not count towards receipt, and the rents cannot be prepaid.” \[G §5.32, p. 3; repeated under Actual Rents, p. 5\]

STD-3.7 This document does not select between STD-3.5 and STD-3.6. When market rent may be used if actual rent is lower, when higher actual rent may be used, and whether the stated documentation is sufficient or further approval is required: Acra confirmation requested → Q-01.

STD-3.8 “If vacant property is being purchased, qualifying rents are taken from the 1007 or 1025 Appraisal report, as applicable, for qualifying income.” Rental income from the purchase of a vacant property requires a 1007 survey if it is the subject of an Acra loan. \[G §5.32, p. 3; §5.30–5.31, p. 4\]

condition.purpose: Verify that a single-family investment property's excessive monthly lease rent is supported as typical for the area.
steps: Initial Document Review: Review the lease agreement and any submitted local rent-support documentation.
Eligibility Verification: Determine whether the property is a single-family investment property with excessive monthly rent payments reflected on the lease.

Validation and Verification: Verify documentation supports that the monthly rent is typical for the area. Acceptable documentation may include classified ads from local newspapers, a 1007 completed by the appraiser, or a market rent survey completed by a local real estate company or rental management company familiar with market rents in the area.
Final Determination: Record whether the rent is supported as typical for the area.
checks: For a single-family investment property with excessive monthly rent payments reflected on the lease, documentation supports that the monthly rent is typical for the area.

outcomes.criterion: The excessive monthly rent is documented as typical for the area.

ledger.clause:
3.3 Rent schedules and rent evidence
STD-3.9 Acra requires the Single-Family Comparable Rent Schedule (FNMA Form 1007) for single family properties on (i) all DSCR qualifying files, (ii) lease-option purchase transactions where the down payment required in §3.45 is generated from excess monthly rent contributions, or (iii) when proposed rental income is being used to qualify. \[G §14.12, p. 4\]

STD-3.10 A 1007 may be from the original appraiser or any state licensed appraiser. \[G §14.12, p. 4\]

STD-3.11 Single family investment properties with excessive monthly rent payments reflected on the lease require documentation supporting that the monthly rent is typical for the area; acceptable documentation may include classified ads from local newspapers, a 1007 completed by the appraiser, or a market rent survey completed by a local real estate company or rental management company familiar with the market rents in the area. \[G §14.12, p. 4\]

STD-3.12 Short-term rental, appraisal form: for properties occupied as a short-term rental, an STRpro or similar appraisal form is acceptable as replacement to a 1007 as long as it is signed by an appropriately licensed appraiser. \[G §14.13, p. 4\]

STD-3.13 Short-term rental, actual rents: “Acra can accept short term rentals with 12-month ledgers from condotel management companies, property managers, AirBnB, VRBO, etcetera as documentation for actual rents.” How a 12-month ledger establishes qualifying rent, and how the receipt and lease conditions of STD-3.6 apply to short-term rentals: Acra confirmation requested → Q-02. \[G §5.32, p. 3; §14.13, p. 4\]

STD-3.14 Short-term rental caps: “Properties qualifying with short-term rentals are limited to 75% & 70% LTV / CLTV for Purchase or Refinance transactions respectively”; the Summary states maximum CLTV 75% (purchase) and 70% (refinance — rate & term and cash-out), minimum FICO 640. \[G §5.32, p. 3; S: Occupancy Type\]

condition.purpose: Verify the No Ratio DSCR 1007 requirement and recognize that actual-rent proof is not required and DSCR is not calculated.
steps: Initial Document Review: Review the appraisal report and any actual-rent documentation submitted.
Eligibility Verification: Determine whether the file uses No Ratio DSCR.

Validation and Verification: Verify a Form 1007 is provided. Do not require proof of actual rents under this provision. Record that DSCR is not calculated. The property may be short-term rental or long-term rental (appropriate pricing applies).
Final Determination: Record whether the No Ratio DSCR documentation requirement is met.
checks: For a No Ratio DSCR file, a Form 1007 is provided and DSCR is not calculated; proof of actual rents is not required.

STD-3.5 Formula: the lesser of annual in-place rent or market rent (STD-3.1). \[G §5.32, p. 3\]

STD-3.6 Note in the same section: “Acra may use the higher of actual or market rents. Where actual rents exceed market rents, then evidence of actual rents must be documented via two (2) consecutive months proof of rental income receipt and lease agreement(s) to continue at a minimum of three (3) months after closing. Note: Security Deposit does not count towards receipt, and the rents cannot be prepaid.” \[G §5.32, p. 3; repeated under Actual Rents, p. 5\]

STD-3.7 This document does not select between STD-3.5 and STD-3.6. When market rent may be used if actual rent is lower, when higher actual rent may be used, and whether the stated documentation is sufficient or further approval is required: Acra confirmation requested → Q-01.

STD-3.8 “If vacant property is being purchased, qualifying rents are taken from the 1007 or 1025 Appraisal report, as applicable, for qualifying income.” Rental income from the purchase of a vacant property requires a 1007 survey if it is the subject of an Acra loan. \[G §5.32, p. 3; §5.30–5.31, p. 4\]

rule.description: Verify the stated DSCR conditions for allowing a first-time homebuyer.

ledger.clause:
STD-4.9 “Acra defines a First Time Home Buyers (‘FTHB’) as an application where all Applicants have never previously owned a home (real property).” \[G §3.13, p. 10\]

STD-4.10 DSCR: Acra allows first-time homebuyers under all of the following: minimum 700 FICO score; maximum 70% CLTV; minimum DSCR of 1.150; maximum loan amount of \$1,000,000; full amortization required, no interest-only programs; impounds required; minimum six months reserves. The Summary states the same conditions: “Minimum 700 FICO: Max 70% CLTV: DSCR ≥ 1.15: Loan amt ≤ \$1MM: NO I/O: Must Impound: Requires 6mos Reserves”. \[G §3.13, p. 10; S: Restrictions\]

STD-4.11 “Where a FTHB is purchasing an Investment property and the loan is qualifying via DTI program, the maximum DTI will be 43.0%.” Noted as a DTI-program provision — Q-14. \[G §3.13, p. 10\]

STD-4.12 §3.12 separately requires at least one guarantor with prior homeownership experience where the borrower is an entity (STD-6.9). How that requirement and the first-time-homebuyer allowance interact: Acra confirmation requested → Q-09.

STD-10.3 Interest Only, 5 Yr / 30 Year Fixed or 5/1 and 7/1 ARM: minimum loan ≥ \$250K; minimum 640 credit score. \[S: Product Requirements\]

STD-10.4 Interest Only, 10 Yr / 40 Year Term: minimum loan ≥ \$250K; minimum 640 credit score; maximum 80% LTV / CLTV; maximum \$3M loan amount. \[S: Product Requirements\]

STD-10.5 Interest-only is not available to first-time homebuyers (STD-4.10), on vacant-property refinances (STD-8.6 and 8.7) or on properties listed for sale (STD-8.9). \[G §3.13, §10.17, §11.5\]

STD-10.6 Interest Only payments are calculated as the amount sufficient to pay the accrued interest on the mortgage monthly at the time of origination, usually for a set term at the beginning of the repayment term; after that term the payments are recast to a fully amortized payment for the balance of the term ending at maturity. Acra calculates the DSCR using the first payment due under the Note (STD-3.2; which payment enters the denominator on an interest-only loan is Q-26). The excerpt's DTI calculation for interest-only loans (first fully amortized payment on the original balance; for an ARM, the highest achievable rate at that payment's due date) is a DTI-program provision — Q-14. \[G §7.5, p. 13\]

ledger.clause:
1.1 Occupancy, purpose and qualification
STD-1.1 Occupancy is investment property (non-owner occupied) only. \[S: Occupancy Type\]

STD-1.2 An investment property is “a one- to four-unit residential dwelling or a unit in a condominium complex or a PUD owned by an individual who does not occupy the dwelling. The dwelling is leased and occupied as a principal year-round residence to individuals other than the owner.” \[G §3.41, p. 11\]

STD-1.3 The Program Summary is listed as “Business Purpose DSCR” on Acra's rate-sheet page. “Where the borrower is qualifying utilizing the subject property's actual or market cashflow under a business purpose transaction, borrower must execute with loan docs a Business Purpose Attestation (Exhibit 8) or other similar attestation approved by Acra.” The excerpt's §8.4 also refers to consumer transactions (STD-9.2); whether every loan on this program is a business-purpose transaction: Acra confirmation requested → Q-27. \[G §5.32, p. 3; acralending.com/ratesheets\]

STD-1.4 The matrix columns are Purchase, Rate & Term and Cash-Out. Delayed financing is addressed only by the matrix footnote “Delayed financing is capped at \$1.5MM”. Which column and which cash-in-hand rule apply to delayed financing: Acra confirmation requested → Q-06. \[S: matrix and footnote\]

STD-1.5 A loan qualifies either by a calculated DSCR (§5.32) or as No Ratio DSCR, where no ratio is calculated (§5.33). Both are set out in section 3. \[G §5.32–5.33, p. 3\]

STD-1.6 “Borrowing entity income documentation not required.” Acra will not calculate a DTI for applicants who qualify using a DSCR; income or employment listed on an application is superfluous to the underwrite and may be left blank, and if represented, a DTI should not be calculated. \[S: Income Documentation; G §7.3, p. 5\]

PLAT-7.6 A property is considered listed for sale under §11.5 if it has been listed for sale in the last six months, measured from (a) the last date of being listed to (b) the Application Date. \[G §11.5, p. 12\]

PLAT-7.7 Whether §11.5 applies to Platinum Select unchanged is part of Q-13; it is restated here because the Platinum Summary does not exclude it. \[G §11.5\]

PLAT-7.8 Loans on such properties will be considered under the following characteristics: the property is not in default or otherwise delinquent on lien(s); for investment properties, the subject must be occupied by a tenant and may not be vacant; the loan must qualify as either (a) ≥ 1.0 DSCR or (b) 43% maximum DTI — on this program the channel minimum DSCR applies, Wholesale 1.0 and Correspondent 1.2 (PLAT-3.8), and the DTI alternative is Q-14; a prepayment penalty of at least three (3) years is required unless the property is in a state that does not allow prepayment penalties; twenty-four (24) months of reserves are required, and cash-in-hand may be considered if otherwise consistent with the Guide; the loan must have a fully amortizing term, interest only is not available; the maximum LTV / CLTV is 65% based on the lesser of (a) appraised value or (b) lowest recent listing price; no subordinate financing is allowed; impounds are required. \[G §11.5, pp. 11–12\]

PLAT-7.7 Whether §11.5 applies to Platinum Select unchanged is part of Q-13; it is restated here because the Platinum Summary does not exclude it. \[G §11.5\]

PLAT-7.8 Loans on such properties will be considered under the following characteristics: the property is not in default or otherwise delinquent on lien(s); for investment properties, the subject must be occupied by a tenant and may not be vacant; the loan must qualify as either (a) ≥ 1.0 DSCR or (b) 43% maximum DTI — on this program the channel minimum DSCR applies, Wholesale 1.0 and Correspondent 1.2 (PLAT-3.8), and the DTI alternative is Q-14; a prepayment penalty of at least three (3) years is required unless the property is in a state that does not allow prepayment penalties; twenty-four (24) months of reserves are required, and cash-in-hand may be considered if otherwise consistent with the Guide; the loan must have a fully amortizing term, interest only is not available; the maximum LTV / CLTV is 65% based on the lesser of (a) appraised value or (b) lowest recent listing price; no subordinate financing is allowed; impounds are required. \[G §11.5, pp. 11–12\]

condition.purpose: Determine whether the loan qualifies as either ≥ 1.0 DSCR or 43% maximum DTI, taking account of the stated channel minimum DSCR and the unresolved DTI alternative question.
steps: Initial Document Review: Review the loan qualification evidence and the applicable channel information.

Eligibility Verification: Apply the stated alternative of ≥ 1.0 DSCR or 43% maximum DTI; the source states that the channel minimum DSCR applies, Wholesale 1.0 and Correspondent 1.2, and identifies the DTI alternative as Q-14.
Validation and Verification: Verify LoanCore.channel and LoanCore.dscr_qualification_method and review the data supporting the applicable qualification method.
Final Determination: Determine whether the listed-property qualification requirement is met, without resolving the DTI alternative beyond the source text.
checks: The loan qualifies as either ≥ 1.0 DSCR, subject to the stated channel minimum DSCR (Wholesale 1.0 and Correspondent 1.2), or 43% maximum DTI, subject to the unresolved Q-14 DTI alternative.

outcomes.criterion: The listed-property qualification requirement is established under the applicable stated alternative.

ledger.clause:
PLAT-8.1 Gift funds, investment property: applicant(s) are required to contribute a portion of their own sourced and seasoned funds to the transaction at a minimum of 10% of the purchase price (PLAT-1.15). \[G §8.7, p. 12\]

PLAT-8.2 Verification of the seasoning of funds to close is required on loans over 70% CLTV for consumer transactions, or business purpose loans where funds to close are over \$50,000 and over 70% CLTV. Whether any loan on this program is a consumer transaction is Q-22. \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

PLAT-8.3 Where the account(s) serving as the source of funds must be verified, verification may include a copy of the borrower's bank statement(s) for the most recent month(s), or a VOD reflecting a current and average balance for the most recent month(s). \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

PLAT-8.4 “All transactions require a minimum of 30-days documentation.” Whether any seasoning period applies to domestic funds beyond this documentation minimum: Acra confirmation requested → Q-11. \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

PLAT-8.5 “In contrast to the above, but consistent with §3.10.1 of this Guide, funds held in a foreign bank / currency will need to be repatriated at minimum three (3) business days prior to Closing”. Foreign nationals are not eligible for this program, but an eligible US citizen or permanent resident may hold funds abroad; the same sentence's 60-day seasoning requirement is stated for Foreign Nationals only and is not restated. Whether the repatriation requirement applies to eligible borrowers holding funds abroad, and what evidence and timing convention apply: Acra confirmation requested → Q-11. \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

PLAT-8.6 “See guidelines for unacceptable source of funds” — the Seller's Guide provision is not reproduced (Appendix B). \[P: Reserve Requirements\]

PLAT-8.2 Verification of the seasoning of funds to close is required on loans over 70% CLTV for consumer transactions, or business purpose loans where funds to close are over \$50,000 and over 70% CLTV. Whether any loan on this program is a consumer transaction is Q-22. \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

PLAT-8.3 Where the account(s) serving as the source of funds must be verified, verification may include a copy of the borrower's bank statement(s) for the most recent month(s), or a VOD reflecting a current and average balance for the most recent month(s). \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

PLAT-8.4 “All transactions require a minimum of 30-days documentation.” Whether any seasoning period applies to domestic funds beyond this documentation minimum: Acra confirmation requested → Q-11. \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

PLAT-8.5 “In contrast to the above, but consistent with §3.10.1 of this Guide, funds held in a foreign bank / currency will need to be repatriated at minimum three (3) business days prior to Closing”. Foreign nationals are not eligible for this program, but an eligible US citizen or permanent resident may hold funds abroad; the same sentence's 60-day seasoning requirement is stated for Foreign Nationals only and is not restated. Whether the repatriation requirement applies to eligible borrowers holding funds abroad, and what evidence and timing convention apply: Acra confirmation requested → Q-11. \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

PLAT-8.6 “See guidelines for unacceptable source of funds” — the Seller's Guide provision is not reproduced (Appendix B). \[P: Reserve Requirements\]

condition.purpose: Determine whether the reserve requirement stated for CLTV over 75.00% is met.
steps: Step 1 - Initial Document Review: Review information establishing CLTV and available reserves.
Step 2 - Eligibility Verification: Determine whether CLTV is over 75.00%.
Step 3 - Validation and Verification: If the trigger applies, verify 6-months Reserves required for CLTV > 75.00%. Do not supply a payment basis not stated in the source.
Step 4 - Final Determination: Record whether the stated reserve requirement is met.
checks: CLTV is over 75.00%.
When CLTV is over 75.00%, 6-months Reserves are available.

There is no case for this outcome.

CLTV is not over 75.00%.

condition.purpose: Determine whether the reserve requirement for the stated forbearance or mortgage-lates and rent-receipt situation is met.
steps: Step 1 - Initial Document Review: Review information establishing forbearance or mortgage lates, occupancy, receipt of the prior two months' rent, and available reserves.

Step 2 - Eligibility Verification: Determine whether the loan has forbearance or mortgage lates in the last 12 months, the subject is tenant-occupied, and the prior two months' rent were not received timely.
Step 3 - Validation and Verification: If all trigger conditions apply, verify 12 months of the subject's payment in reserve. The reserve may be from the transaction's cash-in-hand.
Step 4 - Final Determination: Record whether the stated reserve requirement is met.
checks: Forbearance or mortgage lates in the last 12 months, tenant-occupied subject, and no timely receipt of the prior two months' rent are all present.
When all trigger conditions are present, 12 months of the subject's payment are in reserve.

outcomes.criterion: The stated trigger conditions do not all apply, or they all apply and 12 months of the subject's payment are in reserve.
There is no case for this outcome.
All stated trigger conditions apply and 12 months of the subject's payment are not in reserve.
The stated trigger conditions do not all apply.

missing_reads: Whether forbearance occurred
Whether mortgage lates occurred in the last 12 months
Whether the subject is tenant-occupied
Whether the prior two months' rent were received timely
Subject's payment amount
Reserve amount

rule.description: Apply the stated 12-month subject-payment reserve requirement when all stated rent-receipt trigger conditions apply.

condition.purpose: Determine whether required due diligence and background review are current and cover the specified parties.
steps: Initial Document Review: Review the loan approval or draw date and the borrower / guarantor due-diligence records and background-check results in the loan file.

Eligibility Verification: Verify that borrower / guarantor due diligence is current as of the date of any loan approval or draw. Identify the entity, recourse guarantor(s), and any party (individual or entity) that owns 20% or more of the entity directly or indirectly or has managing control.

Validation and Verification: Review the due-diligence coverage for the identified parties. Acra may order background checks from Checkpoint, LexisNexis or another comparable provider, including criminal history, OFAC searches, litigation, judgment, and lien searches.
Final Determination: Record whether due diligence is current and whether the background review covers the stated parties, as applicable.
checks: Borrower / Guarantor Due Diligence is current as of the date of any loan approval or draw.
The background review covers the entity, recourse guarantor(s), and any party (individual or entity) that owns 20% or more of the entity directly or indirectly or has managing control.

outcomes.criterion: Due diligence is current as of the applicable approval or draw date and the background review covers the stated parties.
There is no case for this outcome.
Due diligence is not current as of the applicable approval or draw date, or the required parties are not covered by the background review.
The borrower is not an entity borrower.

missing_reads: The approval or draw date, due-diligence date, identity of the entity and guarantors, ownership and managing-control information, and background-check results.

rule.description: Verify that borrower and guarantor due diligence is current as of approval or draw and that the applicable key principals and entities are reviewed.

condition.purpose: Determine whether each direct entity owner on title is included as a borrowing entity.
steps: Initial Document Review: Review the title commitment and entity documents to identify each direct owner of the subject property and each entity proposed to appear on title.
Eligibility Verification: For every entity that will hold direct ownership and be on title as a direct owner, verify that it is a borrowing entity.
Validation and Verification: Compare the direct owners shown on the title commitment with the borrowing entities identified in the loan file.
Final Determination: Record whether all entity direct owners on title are borrowing entities.
checks: Every entity that will hold direct ownership of the subject property and will be on title as a direct owner is a borrowing entity.

outcomes.criterion: Every entity direct owner on title is a borrowing entity.
There is no case for this outcome.
At least one entity direct owner on title is not a borrowing entity.

condition.purpose: Determine whether the entity borrower meets the stated entity-type and jurisdiction requirements.

Final Determination: Record whether the entity satisfies the permitted-form and US-formed-and-based requirements.

5.1 Entity eligibility and guarantees
PLAT-5.1 Business Entities are eligible for financing on business purpose transactions (investment properties exclusively). \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.6 Changes to the operating agreement or bylaws with the intent of changing ownership percentages to circumvent required personal guarantors will not be considered. “Lookback to changes cannot occur within 30 days prior to an Application Date or throughout the application process as these changes will not be recognized by Acra Lending.” \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.7 Entity / guarantor types allowed: Domestic Corporations (C and S Corp); single purpose Limited Liability Companies (LLC), excluding series LLC; Limited Liability Partnership (LLP); Limited Liability Limited Partnership (LLLP); General Partnership (GP); Limited Partnership (LP); and Sole Proprietorship. “In all events, the Borrower must be a US formed and based Entity, foreign entities (i.e.: entities formed or based outside the US) or foreign owned entities are not allowed.” \[G §3.12, p. 8\]

condition.purpose: Determine whether the required entity documentation is provided and meets the stated requirements.
steps: Initial Document Review: Obtain and review the complete, legible Certificate of Formation / Articles of Organization and all amendments; the applicable complete Operating Agreement with all referenced exhibits or Bylaws and all amendments; ownership-interest evidence; and any applicable stock certificates, stock ledger, Affidavit of Lost Stock Certificate, K-1 statements, and CPA or Tax Preparer letter. Also review the Certificate of Good Standing or equivalent, any required Certificate of Foreign Qualification or other qualification, IRS Form SS4 or TIN or EIN issuance letter, and the Unanimous Written Consent / Board Resolution.

Eligibility Verification: Verify that the Operating Agreement or Bylaws states whether the entity is member or manager managed, contains authorization to borrow money and enter into contracts for mortgage assets, and designates signers. Verify that ownership interests are evidenced as required: LLCs and Partnerships identify all persons by name with their ownership interest or provide membership interest certificates / units in compliance with the Operating Agreement; S or C Corporations provide compliant shareholder / stockholder certificates or, if unavailable, a stock ledger accounting for all outstanding shares noted in the formation documents, including those held by the corporation. If stock certificates are lost, destroyed, mutilated, or otherwise unavailable, verify an Affidavit of Lost Stock Certificate. For S-corporations or Partnerships where both stock certificate and stock ledger are unavailable, verify the most recent preceding tax year's K-1 statement for all members with 20% or more interest and a letter from the CPA or Tax Preparer affirming current ownership interest, with a statement to that effect if the preceding year's taxes have not been filed.

Validation and Verification: Verify that entity-document names match the identification, or that a letter of explanation addresses any discrepancy; that the Certificate of Good Standing or equivalent is valid within ninety (90) days of the closing date; and that a Certificate of Foreign Qualification or other qualification to operate in the state where business is being conducted is provided if the entity is formed in a state other than where business is performed or where the property is located. Verify that the Unanimous Written Consent / Board Resolution is signed by all members regardless of their percentage of interest, authorizes the transaction with Acra Lending, and identifies who is authorized to sign the loan documents on behalf of and to bind the entity. Verify that it is not used to designate a signor on a personal guarantee. Review any required Power of Attorney for execution of a personal guarantee by an attorney in fact. Do not accept borrower letters stating that required documents are not required, available, or excused from providing them. Additional information may be required if formation documents and the Operating Agreement or Bylaws conflict.

Final Determination: Record whether each applicable required document and requirement is satisfied. Refer any EIN exception request for review by Acra's Legal Department with a letter of explanation stating the applicable grounds; note that Legal reserves the right to condition for additional supporting documentation as determined in its sole discretion.
checks: The required Certificate of Formation / Articles of Organization and all amendments are complete and legible.

The applicable Operating Agreement or Bylaws, including all referenced exhibits and amendments, is complete and legible and contains the required management, borrowing, contract, and signer provisions.
The required ownership-interest evidence is provided and complies with the applicable entity-type requirements.
The entity-document names match the identification, or a letter of explanation addresses any discrepancy.
A Certificate of Good Standing or equivalent is valid within ninety (90) days of the closing date.

If the entity is formed in a state other than where business is performed or where the property is located, a Certificate of Foreign Qualification or other qualification to operate in the state where business is being conducted is provided.

The IRS Form SS4 or Federal Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) or Employer Identification Number (EIN) issuance letter is provided, or an EIN exception request is submitted for review by Acra's Legal Department with a letter of explanation stating the applicable grounds.

A Unanimous Written Consent / Board Resolution signed by all members regardless of their percentage of interest authorizes the transaction with Acra Lending and identifies who is authorized to sign and bind the entity for the loan documents; it is not used to designate a signor on a personal guarantee.
A Power of Attorney is utilized by the principal to designate an attorney in fact to execute a personal guarantee when applicable.
Borrower letters stating that required documents are not required, available, or excused from providing them are not accepted.

outcomes.criterion: Every applicable required entity-document requirement is satisfied.
Acra's Legal Department conditions for additional supporting documentation, or an applicable required document or review remains outstanding subject to a condition that must be cleared.
An applicable required entity-document requirement is not met, or a required document is excused by a borrower letter.
The borrower is not an entity borrower.

5.2 Entity documentation
PLAT-5.10 The documents below are required, without exception, and borrower letters stating that they are not required, available, or excused from providing such documents are not acceptable. \[G §3.12, pp. 8–9\]

- Complete, legible copy of the Certificate of Formation / Articles of Organization and all amendments thereto.

- Complete (with all referenced exhibits), legible copy of the Operating Agreement for LLCs and Partnerships, or Bylaws for corporations, and all amendments, that states whether the entity is member or manager managed, contains authorization to borrow money and enter into contracts for mortgage assets, and designates signers. Additional information may be required if the formation documents and the Operating Agreement or Bylaws conflict.

- All documentation evidencing ownership interests: for LLCs and Partnerships, the Operating Agreement must identify, or attach as an exhibit, all persons by name with their ownership interest, or provide copies of the membership interest certificates / units in compliance with the Operating Agreement.

- For S or C Corporations: shareholder / stockholder certificates that comply with the Bylaws, if any, or, if stock certificates are lost or unavailable, the corporation's stock ledger. The certificate or ledger must account for all outstanding shares noted in the Certificate of Formation / Articles of Organization, including those held by the corporation. If stock certificates are lost, destroyed, mutilated, or otherwise unavailable, an Affidavit of Lost Stock Certificate is required.

- For S-corporations or Partnerships, where both stock certificate and stock ledger are unavailable: (i) the most recent preceding tax year's K-1 statement for all members with 20% or more interest, and (ii) a letter from the CPA or Tax Preparer affirming current ownership interest, with a statement to that effect if the preceding year's taxes have not been filed.

5.2 Entity documentation
- Names on the entity documents must match the identification; if they do not match exactly, a letter of explanation is required to address the discrepancy.

- Certificate of Good Standing or equivalent document valid within ninety (90) days of the closing date.

- Certificate of Foreign Qualification or other qualification to operate in the state where business is being conducted, if the entity is formed in a state other than where business is performed or where the property is located.

- IRS Form SS4 or Federal Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) or Employer Identification Number (EIN) issuance letter for the entity. EIN exception requests may be submitted for review by Acra's Legal Department with a letter of explanation stating the applicable grounds.

- A Unanimous Written Consent / Board Resolution signed by all members regardless of their percentage of interest, (i) authorizing the transaction with Acra Lending and (ii) identifying who is authorized to sign the loan documents on behalf of and to bind the entity. It may be required by the Operating Agreement or Bylaws even where ownership is held by one individual. It cannot be used to designate a signor on a personal guarantee, only an authorized signor for the loan documents signed by the entity.

- A Power of Attorney must be utilized by the principal to designate an attorney in fact to execute a personal guarantee; see §23.5(C), not reproduced (Appendix B).

- Legal reserves the right to condition for additional supporting documentation as determined in its sole discretion.
