condition.purpose: Determine whether title may be vested in the proposed inter vivos revocable trust under the stated requirements.
steps: Initial Document Review: Review the title commitment and a complete, legible copy of the Trust or Certification of Trust. Review any written Acra Senior Management exception and supporting trust documents.

Eligibility Verification: Verify that the Trust or Certification of Trust states the existence and date of the Trust; Trustor(s) and current Trustee(s); Trustee powers; whether the Trust is revocable and, if so, who holds the right to revoke; the names and number of Trustees required to sign; the Trust identification number (a Social Security number or an IRS-issued Tax Identification Number); how title to Trust assets should be taken; and that the Trust has not been revoked, modified, or amended in any manner. Verify that the Trust is valid under the laws of the state in which it is established; is revocable and may be changed or canceled at any time for any reason during a Trustor's lifetime; is established by one or more natural persons solely or jointly and becomes effective during their lifetime; and has as its primary beneficiary the individual(s) establishing the Trust.

Validation and Verification: Verify that written exception by Acra Senior Management is obtained if the Trustor(s) and Trustee(s) are not the same. Verify that the Trust specifies the Trustee's power to hold title and mortgage the property; that the beneficiary need not grant written consent for the Trust to borrow money, or that such consent has been granted in writing for purposes of the mortgage; that there is no unusual risk or impairment to the lender's rights; and that holding title in the Trust does not diminish the lender's rights as a creditor. Review any additional supporting documentation required by Legal.
Final Determination: Record whether every stated trust-title requirement is met; do not approve title vesting in an irrevocable trust.
checks: A complete, legible Trust or Certification of Trust contains every stated required Trust detail.

The Trust is valid under the laws of the state in which it is established, is revocable as defined, is established by one or more natural persons and becomes effective during their lifetime, and has as its primary beneficiary the individual(s) establishing the Trust.
Written exception by Acra Senior Management is obtained if the Trustor(s) and Trustee(s) are not the same.
The Trust specifies the required Trustee powers, beneficiary consent provision, absence of unusual risk or impairment to lender rights, and preservation of the lender's rights as a creditor.
The Trust is not irrevocable.

ledger.clause:
PLAT-5.13 Title vesting in an inter vivos revocable trust is permitted when all of the following requirements are followed. \[G §3.12, pp. 9–10\]

- A complete, legible copy of the Trust, or a Certification of Trust stating: the existence and date of the Trust; the Trustor(s) and the current Trustee(s); the powers of the Trustee; whether the Trust is revocable and, if revocable, who holds the right to revoke; the names and number of the Trustees required to sign on behalf of the Trust; the Trust identification number (a Social Security number or an IRS-issued Tax Identification Number); how title to the Trust assets should be taken; and a statement that the Trust has not been revoked, modified, or amended in any manner.

- The Trust must be valid under the laws of the state in which it is established.

- The Trust must be revocable, meaning it can be changed or canceled at any time for any reason during a Trustor's lifetime. Irrevocable trust is not permitted.

- The Trust must be established by one or more natural persons, solely or jointly (Grantor, Trustor, or Settlor), and must become effective during the lifetime of the person(s) establishing it.

- The primary beneficiary of the Trust must be the individual(s) establishing the Trust.

- Written exception by Acra Senior Management must be obtained if the Trustor(s) and Trustee(s) are not the same.

- The Trust must specify that the Trustee has the power to hold title and mortgage the property; that the beneficiary does not need to grant written consent for the Trust to borrow money, or that such consent has been granted in writing for purposes of the mortgage; that there is no unusual risk or impairment to the lender's rights; and that holding title in the Trust does not diminish the lender's rights as a creditor.

- Legal reserves the right to condition for additional supporting documentation as determined in its sole discretion.

ledger.clause:
5.1 Entity eligibility and guarantees
PLAT-5.1 Business Entities are eligible for financing on business purpose transactions (investment properties exclusively). \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.2 Acra will lend to, and require that title to the collateral be held, either (i) directly by an individual person(s) or (ii) by an entity acceptable to Acra in its sole discretion. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.3 Acra requires all individuals with direct or indirect ownership ≥ 20% to provide a recourse guarantee (Acra approved, or Exhibit 7) in the case of an entity borrower. All recourse is joint and several in the case of multiple guarantors. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.4 An entity borrower must be a single purpose entity (SPE): “an entity with no assets other than residential investment or rental properties; engaged in the business of owning and operating residential investment or rental properties.” Series limited liability companies are not allowed. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.5 All entities that will hold direct ownership of the subject property and will be on title as a direct owner are required to be a borrowing entity. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.6 Changes to the operating agreement or bylaws with the intent of changing ownership percentages to circumvent required personal guarantors will not be considered. “Lookback to changes cannot occur within 30 days prior to an Application Date or throughout the application process as these changes will not be recognized by Acra Lending.” \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.7 Entity / guarantor types allowed: Domestic Corporations (C and S Corp); single purpose Limited Liability Companies (LLC), excluding series LLC; Limited Liability Partnership (LLP); Limited Liability Limited Partnership (LLLP); General Partnership (GP); Limited Partnership (LP); and Sole Proprietorship. “In all events, the Borrower must be a US formed and based Entity, foreign entities (i.e.: entities formed or based outside the US) or foreign owned entities are not allowed.” \[G §3.12, p. 8\]

condition.purpose: Determine the decisioning credit score used for the loan.
steps: Step 1 - Initial Document Review: Review the credit report and, for a loan closing in the name of an entity, the entity and loan application documents for borrower or guarantor scores, ownership percentages, and wage-earner information.
Step 2 - Eligibility Verification: For an individual loan, identify the Primary Wage Earner. For an entity loan, identify the personal guarantors and their ownership percentages.

Step 3 - Validation and Verification: Apply PLAT-6.1: use the Primary Wage Earner middle score for an individual loan; for an entity loan, use the highest middle score of the personal guarantors if ownership percentages are equal, or the individual with the highest concentration of ownership if ownership percentages differ. Do not select a score using a rule not stated in the source where the selection is unresolved.
Step 4 - Final Determination: Record the decisioning credit score if the source specifies how it is selected; otherwise record that Acra confirmation is required under Q-05.
checks: The decisioning credit score is selected according to the applicable selection rule stated in PLAT-6.1.

If the file has one or two scores, no score, no income documentation identifying the Primary Wage Earner, or two or more guarantors with an equal largest ownership interest where ownership is not equal across all guarantors, the unresolved score-selection issue is identified.

condition.purpose: Determine whether required DSCR housing history is documented for the specified properties.
steps: Step 1 - Initial Document Review: Review available credit reports and housing-history documentation for the borrower and / or guarantor(s).

Step 2 - Eligibility Verification: Identify the subject property, primary residence, second homes if applicable, additional properties, and any documents suggesting a major credit event on an additional property.

Step 3 - Validation and Verification: Verify payment history documentation for the primary residence, subject property, and second homes, if applicable. Do not require housing history for additional properties unless documents in the file suggest a major credit event has occurred.
Step 4 - Final Determination: Record whether the required DSCR housing history is documented for the properties within the stated scope.
checks: Payment history is documented for the primary residence, subject property, and second homes, if applicable.

ledger.clause:
PLAT-6.10 The mortgage / rental rating for determining mortgage pricing is determined by evaluating the ratings for properties the borrower owns and / or rents over the last twelve (12) months. All reported mortgages on credit should be considered; where the applicant has mortgages that are not reported, the file should contain documentation to evaluate history on the applicant's primary residence(s), any secondary residence(s), and the subject property. \[G §4.15, p. 5\]

PLAT-6.11 DSCR loans only require documentation on the subject property, principal residence, and second home (if any) of the borrower and / or guarantor(s). Additional properties do not require housing history to be documented unless documents in the file suggest a major credit event has occurred, for example a foreclosure listing the borrower (individually or as guarantor) on the credit report. For DSCR loans, the payment history is required for the primary residence, subject property, and second homes, if applicable. \[G §4.15, p. 5; §6.7, p. 6\]

PLAT-6.12 Loans that have matured are rated based on the maturity date of the loan; any extensions of the maturity date must be in writing. \[G §4.15, p. 5\]

condition.purpose: Determine the mortgage / rental rating for mortgage pricing using the required history scope.
steps: Step 1 - Initial Document Review: Review credit-report mortgage information and available documentation for properties the borrower owns and / or rents over the last twelve (12) months.

Step 2 - Eligibility Verification: Identify all reported mortgages and any mortgages not reported on credit; identify the applicant's primary residence(s), secondary residence(s), and subject property as applicable.

Step 3 - Validation and Verification: Consider all reported mortgages. For mortgages not reported, verify that the file contains documentation to evaluate history on the applicant's primary residence(s), any secondary residence(s), and the subject property.

Step 4 - Final Determination: Determine the mortgage / rental rating for mortgage pricing by evaluating the applicable ratings for properties the borrower owns and / or rents over the last twelve (12) months.
checks: All reported mortgages on credit are considered in evaluating the mortgage / rental rating.
For any mortgage not reported on credit, the file contains documentation to evaluate history on the applicant's primary residence(s), any secondary residence(s), and the subject property.
The mortgage / rental rating for mortgage pricing is determined by evaluating ratings for properties the borrower owns and / or rents over the last twelve (12) months.

ledger.clause:
PLAT-6.10 The mortgage / rental rating for determining mortgage pricing is determined by evaluating the ratings for properties the borrower owns and / or rents over the last twelve (12) months. All reported mortgages on credit should be considered; where the applicant has mortgages that are not reported, the file should contain documentation to evaluate history on the applicant's primary residence(s), any secondary residence(s), and the subject property. \[G §4.15, p. 5\]

PLAT-6.11 DSCR loans only require documentation on the subject property, principal residence, and second home (if any) of the borrower and / or guarantor(s). Additional properties do not require housing history to be documented unless documents in the file suggest a major credit event has occurred, for example a foreclosure listing the borrower (individually or as guarantor) on the credit report. For DSCR loans, the payment history is required for the primary residence, subject property, and second homes, if applicable. \[G §4.15, p. 5; §6.7, p. 6\]

PLAT-6.12 Loans that have matured are rated based on the maturity date of the loan; any extensions of the maturity date must be in writing. \[G §4.15, p. 5\]

condition.purpose: Determine whether the stated rental-payment or reserve documentation is present when the provision applies.
steps: Step 1 - Initial Document Review: Review the credit report and available rental-payment or reserve documentation.
Step 2 - Eligibility Verification: Determine whether the Applicant has had forbearance or mortgage lates within the last 12-months and whether the property is tenant occupied.

Step 3 - Validation and Verification: Where the stated provision applies, verify documentation of either timely receipt for the prior two (2) months rental payments or 12-months of subject's payment in reserve, which may be from transaction's cash-in-hand. Record that the source does not state how this provision relates to the Platinum Summary's “0x30x12” housing history requirement, which cases it covers, or whether “Applicant” includes guarantors of an entity borrower; Acra confirmation is requested under Q-17.
Step 4 - Final Determination: Record whether the applicable documentation alternative is present and identify any unresolved applicability question.

condition.purpose: Determine whether the applicant meets the stated tradeline and history requirement.
steps: Step 1 - Initial Document Review: Review the credit report for repository scores, tradelines, and credit history.
Step 2 - Eligibility Verification: Determine whether the applicant has scores from 3 repositories or 2 or fewer scores; treat an applicant with one score as within “2 or fewer scores”.

Step 3 - Validation and Verification: For scores from 3 repositories, verify the stated no-tradeline-overlay rule. For 2 or fewer scores, verify either 2 tradelines & 24 month history or 3 tradelines & 12 month history.
Step 4 - Final Determination: Record whether the applicable tradeline requirement is met. Do not infer a decisioning-score rule or a no-score pathway from this tradeline provision.
checks: If the applicant has scores from 3 repositories, the no-tradeline-overlay rule applies; otherwise, the applicant has 2 tradelines & 24 month history or 3 tradelines & 12 month history.

ledger.clause:
PLAT-6.1 “Decisioning Credit Score: Primary Wage Earner middle score. For loans that close in the name of an entity, use the highest middle score of the personal guarantors, presuming equal percentages of ownership. If ownership percentages differ, use the individual with the highest concentration of ownership.” \[P: Borrower Credit History Requirements\]

PLAT-6.2 Minimum decisioning score 700 (no matrix row below 700, PLAT-2.1); Correspondent pricing limited to 60% CLTV for 700-719 (PLAT-2.3). \[P: matrix; footnote 3\]

PLAT-6.3 “Tradelines: Applicants with scores from 3 repositories are deemed to be acceptable with no tradeline overlay. 2 tradelines & 24 month history or 3 tradelines & 12 month history for applicants with 2 or fewer scores.” \[P: Borrower Credit History Requirements\]

PLAT-6.4 Applicants with one score are within “2 or fewer scores” for the tradeline requirement above. The Platinum Summary does not state how the decisioning score is set with one score or with two scores, whether any no-score pathway exists, or how “Primary Wage Earner” is identified on a file with no income documentation. The Standard Summary's one-or-no-score provision is not restated here: Acra confirmation requested → Q-05. \[P: Borrower Credit History Requirements\]

PLAT-6.5 Where two or more guarantors hold an equal largest ownership interest and ownership is not equal across all guarantors, PLAT-6.1 does not say whose score is used: Acra confirmation requested → Q-05. \[P: Borrower Credit History Requirements\]

condition.purpose: Establish whether the borrower is a US Citizen or Permanent Resident, or has a citizenship status that is not eligible under the listed types.
steps: Step 1 - Initial Document Review: Review the loan application for the borrower's citizenship status.
Step 2 - Eligibility Verification: Compare the borrower's citizenship status with the listed eligible types: US Citizen and Permanent Resident.
Step 3 - Validation and Verification: Confirm that the case's citizenship-status value is consistent with the reviewed information.
Step 4 - Final Determination: Record whether the borrower's citizenship status is a listed eligible type.
checks: Borrower citizenship status is US Citizen or Permanent Resident.

rule.description: Determine whether the borrower's citizenship status is one of the eligible types listed for the program.

ledger.clause:
The Platinum Summary lists two eligible citizenship types and excludes first-time homebuyers. Borrowing entities, guarantors and trusts follow the Seller's Guide excerpt and are in section 5.

PLAT-4.1 Eligible borrower citizenship types: US Citizen, Permanent Resident. \[P: Borrower Citizenship Requirements\]

PLAT-4.2 Permanent Resident must have an unexpired PRA ID and SSA card / SSA-89. \[P: Borrower Citizenship Requirements\]

PLAT-4.3 Non-permanent residents, foreign nationals and ITIN borrowers are not among the listed eligible types. The Seller's Guide foreign-national program (§3.10) is therefore not restated (Appendix B). \[P: Borrower Citizenship Requirements\]

PLAT-4.4 “First Time Homebuyer (FTHB) ineligible for this program”. Acra defines a First Time Home Buyer as “an application where all Applicants have never previously owned a home (real property)”; the §3.13 DSCR allowance for first-time homebuyers is not restated (Appendix B). \[P: Borrower Credit History Requirements; G §3.13, p. 10\]

PLAT-4.5 §3.12 requires at least one guarantor to have prior homeownership experience, and at least one borrower / guarantor to attest on the application that they are not a first-time homebuyer (PLAT-5.9). Whether it applies to individual borrowers as well as entities is part of Q-13. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

condition.purpose: Determine whether the loan meets the applicable minimum DSCR for its channel.
steps: Step 1 - Initial Document Review: Review available rent evidence and payment information relevant to the DSCR calculation.
Step 2 - Eligibility Verification: Identify the loan channel and verify that the file is being qualified using DSCR.

Step 3 - Validation and Verification: Determine qualifying rent using the greater of market rent established on the 1007 or 1025, or actual rent. Calculate the denominator using annual PITIA and, if applicable, subordinate financing; use the first payment due under the terms of the Note.
Step 4 - Final Determination: Compare the calculated DSCR with the applicable channel minimum: Correspondent ≥ 1.2; Wholesale ≥ 1.0.
checks: The DSCR, calculated using the stated qualifying-rent and denominator rules, meets the applicable channel minimum: Correspondent ≥ 1.2 or Wholesale ≥ 1.0.

1.1 Occupancy, purpose and qualification
PLAT-1.7 The program is offered through two channels with different minimum ratios: Correspondent ≥ 1.2, Wholesale ≥ 1.0 (PLAT-3.7). Matrix footnote 3 also restricts Correspondent pricing (PLAT-2.3). \[P: Minimum DSCR; matrix footnote 3\]

PLAT-1.8 Every loan must meet the applicable channel minimum DSCR. The Platinum Summary lists no No Ratio option and no allowance for a ratio below 1.0; a ratio below the channel minimum does not meet the published requirement. Whether No Ratio or sub-1.0 qualification exists on this program in any form: Acra confirmation requested → Q-12. \[P: Minimum DSCR\]

PLAT-1.9 Acra will not calculate a DTI for applicants who qualify using a DSCR; income or employment listed on an application is superfluous to the underwrite and may be left blank, and if represented, a DTI should not be calculated. The Standard Summary's statement that borrowing-entity income documentation is not required does not appear in the Platinum Summary; whether it applies: Acra confirmation requested → Q-13. \[G §7.3, p. 5\]

PLAT-1.10 “A 1007 will always be required on DSCR transactions”; the Platinum Summary refers to market rent “as established on the 1007 or 1025”. Whether a Form 1025 alone satisfies the requirement for a two-unit property: Acra confirmation requested → Q-04. \[G §5.32, p. 3; §14.12, p. 4; P: Income Documentation\]

PLAT-1.11 All borrowers purchasing or refinancing a one- to four-family investment property must execute a One- to Four-Family Rider with the loan documents and provide rent loss insurance coverage per §23.40 (PLAT-7.9 to 7.12). \[G §3.41, p. 11\]

PLAT-1.12 Only the subject property, principal residence and second homes are required to be listed on the application or Schedule of Real Estate Owned. \[G §5.32, p. 3; §4.15, p. 5\]

PLAT-3.1 “When calculating the DSCR, Acra will use the greater of the market rent as established on the 1007 or 1025, or actual rent. When using actual rent, the actual rent must be documented via evidence of 2 months’ proof of receipts and the lease must be in place for at least 3 months after the loan closing. This applies to long-term rents only and is not appropriate for short-term rentals.” \[P: Income Documentation & Debt Ratio Requirements\]

PLAT-3.2 §5.32 of the excerpt states the general formula as “the lesser of (i) annual in-place rent or (ii) market rent”, then notes that “Acra may use the higher of actual or market rents” subject to “two (2) consecutive months proof of rental income receipt”, a lease continuing at least three months after closing, and: “Security Deposit does not count towards receipt, and the rents cannot be prepaid.” The Platinum Summary's statement (PLAT-3.1) is program-specific; the excerpt's general formula is reproduced here. Which governs Platinum Select and how they relate, whether “2 months’ proof of receipts” means consecutive months, and whether the security-deposit and prepaid-rent conditions apply: Acra confirmation requested → Q-03. \[G §5.32, p. 3\]

PLAT-3.3 Short-term rentals are ineligible for the program (PLAT-7.2); the Seller's Guide provisions on short-term rental income and appraisal forms are not restated (Appendix B). \[P: Subject Property Requirements\]

PLAT-3.4 Denominator, per §5.32: “the sum of annual principal, interest, real estate taxes, property insurance, and homeowner's / condominium association fees (collectively, ‘PITIA’). Subordinate financing, if applicable, would also be included in the denominator for the sake of this calculation.” \[G §5.32, p. 3\]

PLAT-3.5 “Acra calculates the DSCR utilizing the first payment due under the terms of the Note.” §7.5 defines Interest Only payments as “the amount sufficient to pay the accrued interest to the mortgage on a monthly basis at the time of origination”, while the §5.32 denominator lists “annual principal, interest …”. Which payment enters the DSCR denominator on an interest-only loan: Acra confirmation requested → Q-21. \[G §7.5, p. 13; §5.32, p. 3\]

PLAT-3.6 The reference to subordinate financing in the denominator is a calculation rule; it does not itself establish that a subordinate lien is permitted. The Platinum Summary does not address subordinate financing or restate the Standard Summary's HELOC calculation: Acra confirmation requested → Q-15. \[G §5.32, p. 3\]

PLAT-3.7 Minimum Debt Service Coverage Ratio: Correspondent ≥ 1.2; Wholesale ≥ 1.0. \[P: Minimum DSCR\]

PLAT-3.8 Property listed for sale within six months (§11.5): the excerpt requires “≥1.0 DSCR”; on this program the channel minimum applies — Wholesale 1.0, Correspondent 1.2 (PLAT-7.8). \[G §11.5, p. 11; P: Minimum DSCR\]

PLAT-3.1 “When calculating the DSCR, Acra will use the greater of the market rent as established on the 1007 or 1025, or actual rent. When using actual rent, the actual rent must be documented via evidence of 2 months’ proof of receipts and the lease must be in place for at least 3 months after the loan closing. condition.purpose: Determine whether the loan meets the applicable printed FICO and CLTV limits.
steps: Initial Document Review: Review the credit report and loan application for representative score, loan purpose, channel, and CLTV.

Eligibility Verification: Apply the matrix printed for loan amounts ≤ $2,000,000: at 730, Purchase 80%, Rate & Term 80%, Cash-Out 75%; at 721, Purchase 80%, Rate & Term 80%, Cash-Out 65%; at 700, Purchase 80%, Rate & Term 80%, Cash-Out 55%. For Correspondent Pricing at 700-719 FICO, also apply the printed 60% CLTV limit; it does not raise a lower matrix limit.

Validation and Verification: Verify the score, purpose, channel, and CLTV against the credit report, application, and case information. For a score of exactly 720, obtain Acra confirmation on its treatment rather than assigning a matrix row.
Final Determination: Record whether the applicable limits are met or whether Acra confirmation is required for a score of exactly 720.
checks: For a score covered by a printed matrix row, CLTV does not exceed the row's maximum for the loan purpose.
For Correspondent Pricing with a score of 700-719, CLTV is ≤ 60%.
For a score of exactly 720, Acra confirmation on its treatment has been obtained.

outcomes.criterion: The applicable matrix check and, when applicable, the Correspondent check hold; if the score is exactly 720, Acra confirmation has been obtained and its treatment is satisfied.
The score is exactly 720 and Acra confirmation on its treatment is pending.

PLAT-2.1 The rows below are Acra's. Each row is a minimum-FICO threshold: a score at or above the threshold and below the next higher threshold takes that row. No row is printed below 700. \[P: Loan Amount, FICO, CLTV Requirements\] | **Min FICO** | **Purchase** | **Rate & Term** | **Cash-Out** | |--------------|--------------|-----------------|--------------| | 730 | 80% | 80% | 75% | | 721 | 80% | 80% | 65% | | 700 | 80% | 80% | 55% |

THE PRINTED 721 THRESHOLD AND A SCORE OF 720

PLAT-9.6 Interest Only payments are calculated as the amount sufficient to pay the accrued interest on the mortgage monthly at the time of origination, usually for a set term at the beginning of the repayment term; after that term the payments are recast to a fully amortized payment for the balance of the term ending at maturity. import rules_lib

def check(ctx):
    property_type = ctx['SubjectProperty.property_type']
    missing = rules_lib.gaps(property_type=property_type)
    if missing:
        return rules_lib.unknown(*missing)
    return rules_lib.same(
        property_type,
        'SFR',
        'Townhome',
        'PUD',
        'Warrantable Condo',
        'Non-Warrantable Condo',
        'Condotel / PUDtel',
        '2-4 Units',
        'Manufactured',
    )

import rules_lib

def check(ctx):
    representative_score = ctx['CreditReport.representative_score']
    interest_only_value = ctx['MortgageLoanInformation.is_interest_only']
    escrow_waived_value = ctx['LoanCore.is_escrow_waived']
    reserves_months = ctx['RatioSet.reserves_months']

    interest_only = rules_lib.flag(interest_only_value)
    escrow_waived = rules_lib.flag(escrow_waived_value)
    missing = rules_lib.gaps(
        representative_score=representative_score,
        interest_only=interest_only,
        escrow_waived=escrow_waived,
        reserves_months=reserves_months,
    )
    if missing:
        return rules_lib.unknown(*missing)

    return (
        representative_score >= 700
        and not interest_only
        and not escrow_waived
        and reserves_months >= 6
    )

evidence.excerpt:
SKILL: Verify the conditions stated for a vacant property's cash-out refinance and obtain Acra confirmation for unresolved loan-amount and ownership-measurement questions.
PURPOSE: Determine whether a vacant property's cash-out refinance meets the conditions stated in STD-8.7.
CHECKS TO ENCODE:
  - For a vacant property's cash-out refinance, representative FICO score is at least 700.
  - For a vacant property's cash-out refinance, the loan is not interest-only.
  - For a vacant property's cash-out refinance, impounds are in place.
  - For a vacant property's cash-out refinance, reserves are at least 6 months.
CHECKS LEFT TO A REVIEWER:
  - For a vacant property's cash-out refinance, DSCR is at least 1.15.
  - For a vacant property's cash-out refinance, a prepayment penalty of at least 3 years is in place where allowable.
  - For a vacant property's cash-out refinance with a loan amount under $1,500,000, CLTV does not exceed 60%; obtain Acra confirmation for loans of $1,500,000 or more.
  - For a vacant property's cash-out refinance, ownership is at least 15 months; obtain Acra confirmation on how the 15 months are measured.
SOURCE CLAUSE:
STD-8.5 A vacant property may be purchased; qualifying rents are taken from the 1007 or 1025 (STD-3.8). “Vacant investment properties are only eligible for a refinance transaction if consistent with §10.17.” \[G §5.32, p. 3; §3.41, p. 11\]

STD-8.6 Rate and term refinance of a vacant property (§10.17): minimum 700 FICO score; maximum \$1,000,000 to maximum 70% CLTV; maximum \$2,000,000 to maximum 65% CLTV; minimum 1.000 DSCR or maximum 40.0% DTI (Q-14); minimum two-year prepayment penalty (where allowable); full amortization required, no interest-only programs; impounds required; minimum six months reserves. The Summary states the same conditions with “Max CLTV 70% for loan amounts under \$1,000,000 and 65% for loan amounts under \$2,000,000”. Treatment at exactly \$1,000,000 and \$2,000,000: Acra confirmation requested → Q-10. \[G §10.17, p. 11; S: Occupancy Type\]

STD-8.7 Cash-out refinance of a vacant property: the “Cash-Out Refinances” heading in §10.17 is empty in the excerpt. The Summary states: minimum 700 FICO; DSCR ≥ 1.15; ≥ 3-year PPP (where allowable); no interest only; impounds required; 6 months reserves; “Max CLTV 60% for loan amounts under \$1,500,000”; “Requires ≥15 months ownership”. condition.source:
import rules_lib

def check(ctx):
    occupancy = ctx['SubjectProperty.occupancy_subtype']
    state = ctx['SubjectProperty.state']
    missing = rules_lib.gaps(occupancy=occupancy, state=state)
    if missing:
        return rules_lib.unknown(*missing)

    if rules_lib.same(occupancy, 'non-owner-occupied'):
        ineligible_state = rules_lib.same(
            state,
            'SD',
            'Puerto Rico', 'PR',
            'Guam', 'GU',
            'U.S. Virgin Islands', 'US Virgin Islands', 'VI',
            'American Samoa', 'AS',
            'Northern Mariana Islands', 'MP',
        )
        return not ineligible_state
    return True

proposals.reasoning: Applies the printed matrix rows literally: scores 700–720 use the 700 row, 721–729 use the 721 row, and 730 or above use the 730 row. Scores below 700 have no printed matrix row. PLAT-9.3 “Interest-Only (5 Yr Term), Max CLTV: 75.00%”. \[P: Product Requirements — Restrictions\]

PLAT-9.4 No minimum loan amount or minimum FICO is printed for interest-only loans on Platinum Select: Acra confirmation requested → Q-09. \[P: Product Requirements\]

PLAT-9.6 Interest Only payments are calculated as the amount sufficient to pay the accrued interest on the mortgage monthly at the time of origination, usually for a set term at the beginning of the repayment term; after that term the payments are recast to a fully amortized payment for the balance of the term ending at maturity. The excerpt's DTI calculation for interest-only loans is a DTI-program provision — Q-14. \[G §7.5, p. 13\]

proposals.reasoning: For an interest-only loan, the source sets a maximum CLTV of 75.00% and disallows properties listed for sale. CLTV is given in percent, so it is compared directly with 75.00. Non-interest-only loans are not subject to these two checks. Missing or unusable required values are reported as unknown rather than treated as a failure.
